Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Mobile money generates government revenue via sector-specific taxation: reporting notes Cameroon’s 2022 finance law introduced a 0.2% levy on mobile money transfers and withdrawals (with some exemptions), indicating digital payments are a revenue source.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source concerned a tax ON mobile money transactions, not whether taxes can be PAID via digital payment — a mismatch. Verified via Cameroon's tax authority (DGI): the OTP portal (otp.dgi.cm) and TRESORPAY platform, plus Mobile Tax via Orange Money and MTN MoMo, allow online/mobile payment of IRPP, VAT, corporate tax, property tax, patente and customs/excise duties (guide dated May 2026; MINFI Decision 00000337/2024 Art.26 authorises PSPs as tax-payment channels). This is comprehensive, not partial, so upgraded to Yes (3).

Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Cross-border functionality exists at least regionally within CEMAC through GIMACPAY’s interoperable ecosystem (CEMAC-wide), enabling cross-border transactions within the monetary union; however, no confirmation found for PAPSS being integrated/operational in Cameroon, so score reflects regional (not pan-African) coverage.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited SIIPS2023 report itself states GIMACPAY has been fully operational since July 2020 and 'treats domestic and cross-border transactions within the monetary union equally' — the original 'Planned' code did not match its own source. PAPSS network coverage data (June 2026) shows Cameroon reachable only via PAPSS's Extended Network for inbound transactions, not as a full participant. Recodes to Partially functional (4): fully live for CEMAC cross-border, only indirect/partial pan-African (PAPSS) reach.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: G2P evidence exists: World Bank documents Cameroon’s first digital G2P experience via an emergency cash transfer program (COVID-19 response) with beneficiaries preferring receipt into mobile money accounts (digital G2P payments).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed, freshened. A 2022 decree enabled digital G2P/P2G payments and the Adaptive Safety Net project has since piloted digital transfers in urban and some rural areas (reaching a fraction of the ~372,500 cumulative PFS households). A new World Bank-backed G2Px reform using the Tresopay platform to digitise salaries, pensions and social transfers only began national rollout in May 2026. Use remains real but partial rather than active/systemic, so Limited Use (2) is retained.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Consumer protection/redress mechanisms exist through CNEF (national financial education/mediation under BEAC) and financial sector supervision (incl. COBAC); UNCDF highlights CNEF consumer protection functions and mediation/complaints handling.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: CNEF is a general financial-consumer mediation body (CEMAC Regulation 03/2019), not a dedicated payment consumer-protection regime. A 2022 peer-reviewed legal analysis and a subsequent 2024 review both conclude Cameroon's mobile-money consumer protection is insufficient and lacks comprehensive, payment-specific disclosure/liability/dispute-resolution provisions. Per the metadata definition this matches 'Partial' (general consumer law, no payment-specific rules) rather than 'Yes'; downgraded to 2.

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: BEAC annual reporting provides recurring payment-system performance statistics (regional payment infrastructure volumes/values, including SYGMA/SYSTAC/GIMAC-related reporting) but not always at highly granular system-SLA level for Cameroon alone, supporting a mid-to-high score.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and refreshed. BEAC publishes a detailed annual 'Rapport sur les Services de Paiement dans la CEMAC' (latest covering 2024 data, released 2026) with providers, accounts, transaction volumes/values by instrument, plus SYGMA/SYSTAC tables in its Annual Report. No evidence found of more frequent (monthly/quarterly) public reporting, so Annual (3) is retained.

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: Mobile money active users are high: BEAC-reported figures (as relayed in reputable business press) indicate active users increased from 14.8 million (2022) to 17.08 million (2023) in Cameroon, implying very large uptake.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original score conflated total registered mobile-money ACCOUNTS (30.9 million in 2024 per BEAC, which exceeds Cameroon's adult population) with the % of adults actively transacting in the past 90 days — accounts substantially over-count due to multiple registrations per person. The World Bank Global Findex 2025 (2024 survey year), the authoritative demand-side source, puts adults who 'made or received a digital payment' at c.59.6%, and separately confirms Cameroon as a country where digital merchant-payment adoption roughly doubled 2021–24 from a lower base. This places usage in the 50–69% band, so revised to 3.

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: Government adoption is evidenced via the government-run emergency cash transfer program using digital G2P payments into mobile money accounts (COVID-19 response), but evidence of broad government-wide adoption across multiple services is limited in the sources captured, so scored mid-range.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: No authoritative source gives an actual percentage of G2P payments made digitally; the cited World Bank report covers only an 80,000-household pilot, not government-wide disbursement. A 2026 article confirms the World Bank-backed G2Px/Tresopay reform to digitise salaries, pensions and social transfers only began national rollout in May 2026, implying digitisation is still emerging rather than mid-range. Original 50-69% appears to be an unsupported guess; recoded to 0 (Unknown) pending a verifiable figure — flagged for human review.
